title: The Last Apprentice
text: A boy has tended the dead forge alone for years, sweeping, oiling and banking the coals while he waits for his master to come back. He is thin as wire, his eyes too old. He wants to show someone his work. He has made a great many blades.

options.label: The strongest tests his blades, so that someone finally sees his work.

outcomes.text: The work is good. He beams, and for the first time in years the forge feels warm.

options.label: Offer him a place in the House, and a reason to leave.

outcomes.text: He packs his hammer and looks back once. He does not cry.
He shakes his head; he will wait for his master, as he always has.

options.label: Tell him his master is dead. He deserves to know.

outcomes.text: He lets the fire go out and sits in the dark without a word. When you go, you take what iron he will no longer need.
